correctness.rationale: Induct on marked positions: initial marks are 0,2. For a power a=2^k with latest mark 3a−1, every newly appended suffix through index 6a−2 has an earlier occurrence beginning at index a; any new factor must cross the last mark or be inside such a suffix, and is therefore attracted by induction. At index 6a−1 the first run of 2a consecutive zeros appears beyond all prior marks and forces the next mark. This establishes both directions for all k; counting positions below N gives the exact closed form. Independent direct-factor and novel-suffix finite checks and 24,573 scale identities corroborate the steps but are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The identical power-of-two indicator is studied for offline attractors by Schaeffer–Shallit, and a general canonical greedy rule appears in their Definition 19. Their bounds and explicit noncanonical sets do not fix the selected greedy positions. Whittington identifies the exact LZ variant that is equivalent, but does not compute its parsing for the indicator. The newer full-text study using a different greedy algorithm and its same-word numerical table do not imply the online geometric positions. Targeted mathematical-record and literature searches found no statement implying this theorem; a possible unindexed LZ-equivalent remains an explicit bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: The powers-of-two characteristic word is a standard binary automatic stress case with optimal attractor complexity Theta(log N). An explicit canonical online attractor removes the existing constant-factor ambiguity for this natural deterministic rule, yields an exact all-prefix cost and geometric location classification, and equivalently determines every self-referencing novel LZ phrase end for this word. These are useful exact structural data about online compression rather than an arbitrary finite cutoff, while making no claim to solve the harder offline optimum.
